name: KEARNEY, the Hon. Gerardine (Ged) Mary

headline.note: Direct first-person evidence establishes full-time nursing at Austin, but its endpoints and leave periods are unresolved. The later nursing education and union transition dates also conflict. No defensible public/private numerical total yet.

career_spells.evidence_note: Hospital-based training involved work and a childbirth interruption. Qualified RN in 1985; qualification is not an employment endpoint. Sisters of Mercy health service excluded as nonprofit, not private enterprise. Paid-trainee terms and exact dates unresolved.

career_spells.evidence_note: Direct accounts establish full-time shift nursing and nursing during honorary union service. Public hospital identity is supported by contemporaneous public-sector/privatisation evidence. A 2024 ministerial statement places Austin work in the 1980s, but does not establish appointment boundaries. Endpoints, changes in hours and leave remain unknown; do not apply full-time status to an invented 15-year or rounded 20-year interval. The 2019 union interview corroborates full-time nursing during honorary presidencies, but no exact continuous interval.
career_spells.counting_note: Dates, employer control and/or substantive full-time status remain insufficient for a duration calculation; unknown is not zero.

research_notes: Follow-up: locate Austin personnel/annual reports, including the Cowin name variant, for complete nursing dates, hours changes and leave; reconcile the 2002/2003 transition to paid ANF work; identify any additional acute-sector employers and board tenure dates.

2026-09-29: examined indexed APH biography/first speech, ACTU 2010 primary biography and first-person work-life speech, ANMF histories, contemporaneous authored biography, HESTA annual reports and hospital ownership history. Full-time nursing evidence found, but not complete dated intervals.

The 15-year public-sector description in the 2008 author bio is a rounded retrospective without endpoints, and does not establish that every year was full-time or leave-free. Do not subtract 15 from the 2002/2003 union transition to invent a start date.

Training interruption: first speech describes a return seven weeks after childbirth. Start of leave and calendar dates are unknown. Other family-related breaks or hour changes are not established; do not assume none. Nursing registration in 1985 and education degree are study/qualification evidence rather than separate jobs.

2026-09-29: searched historical Austin annual-report catalogues, full-time nursing terms, Cbus appointment records and Skills Australia board leads. Retrieved catalogues did not resolve the historical personnel dates. HESTA annual report confirms resignation, but Cbus/Skills appointment endpoints remain follow-up work.

Potential early family hotel work is not established from the father's occupation and is not entered as employment. Public/private sector descriptions in biographies do not override nonprofit employer classification. All headline totals remain null; overlapping nursing and union roles are not additive.

Follow-up2026-10-02: regulator-held union return and7 April2003 submission narrow the observed president-to-assistant-secretary transition; preserved2002/2003 source conflict. Cbus resignation month resolved. Added1993 workplace representative role separately.

Follow-up2026-10-03: current first-person biography adds previously omitted aged-care nursing and a government ministerial statement places Austin work in the1980s. Neither identifies an aged-care provider or supplies appointment boundaries. The rounded 20-year nursing description is not converted to a continuous full-time duration.

Searched Austin/Cowin historical records and employer/union/government reports. ANMJ2019 says trained at Austin, whereas direct first speech identifies Mercy; do not replace stronger first-person training account. PUPPS2004 article acknowledgement naming Cowin on a working group is a follow-up lead, not proof of employment.

APH submission direct open Internal Error and AWPA report403; official indexed cover usable. No exact nursing start/cessation, aged-care employer, hours changes or leave recovered. Next:2003 election/appointment result and Austin cessation record; aged-care provider; earliest Cbus/HESTA appointments; Skills Australia/AWPA appointment terms.

Follow-up2026-10-04: Kearney's public professional profile refines the later Austin Health employment envelope to January1999–April2003 (4 years 4 months), surrounding the official2000–2002 deputy-director range. This materially improves boundaries but does not establish title-transition days, full-time continuity, hours or leave and cannot be applied to her separately evidenced Austin nursing in the1980s. Aged-care provider identity and earlier nursing boundaries remain unresolved.
